extracted.intended_audience: artists, patrons, and readers of Renaissance art / art historians
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and evaluative criteria for judging Renaissance painters (composition, colour, draughtsmanship, invention, execution), drawn from Vasari's artist biographies and applied examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouping and composition of figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures should be 'well grouped' so the composition reads clearly and harmoniously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vasari praises works where 'his figures are well grouped'; grouping contributes to clarity and overall impact. Examples: the principal door with a seated woman raising a head, figures arranged to communicate a subject. Anti-pattern: disorganized placement that confuses the narrative or visual flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vivacity and harmony of colouring
rubrics_metrics.description: Colours should be lively, harmonious, and contribute to the work's vivacity—'most vivacious in colouring' and 'colouring sweet and full of grace'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeated praise for 'lovely colouring' (fresco and oils) and 'harmony and gradation of the colours'. Scoring notes: evaluation based on chromatic harmony, tonal gradation, and emotional effect of palette. Anti-pattern: flat or discordant colouring lacking subtle gradation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faithfulness to nature / naturalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Work aims 'to be faithful to nature, without any imitation of another's manner'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vasari values direct observation and natural truth over slavish imitation. Examples: truthful portraits, natural gestures and facial expressions (e.g., the smiling child that makes viewers smile). Anti-pattern: mannered copying of another artist's style rather than observation from life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and inventiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Artist should display personal invention and novel conceits—e.g., Giorgione's device proving painting can show multiple aspects, Piero's fantastical monsters and the Car of Death.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vasari asserts worth for 'ingenious and beautiful' inventions and bizarre fantasies. Scoring notes: reward imaginative solutions, theatrical spectacle, and novel visual metaphors. Anti-pattern: derivative or predictable ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to represent multiple aspects / complex viewpoint effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Painting may aim to show various aspects of a subject at one glance (profiles, front, back) through compositional devices (reflections, armour, mirrors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Giorgione painted a nude with back shown, pool reflection of the front, an armour piece showing one profile, and a mirror showing the other—used to argue painting's superiority to sculpture. Evaluate ingenuity and clarity of such devices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Draughtsmanship (drawing skill)
rubrics_metrics.description: Strong drawing from life and precise draughtsmanship are essential—'drew most excellently from the life' and 'heads reveal both draughtsmanship and grace'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vasari contrasts those 'who draw divinely well' but may lack in colour. Scoring should treat accurate anatomy, proportion, and expressive line as core strengths. Anti-pattern: weak draftsmanship undermining forms despite good colour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Colour handling and modelling (flesh, hair, relief)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mastery of colour to model form, produce soft flesh, hair detail, and relief—'no one ever handled colours better', 'softness of his flesh-painting', 'hair so lovely in colour'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess painters on ability to make colour read as flesh and material (e.g., shadows making flesh look like flesh rather than paint). Includes fine work on hair and small features. Anti-pattern: colour that fails to convey material plausibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of drawing and colouring
rubrics_metrics.description: The highest perfection combines excellent colouring with draughtsmanship in every executed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vasari notes painters who excel in one and falter in the other; ideal works unite both. Scoring: penalize imbalance where drawing and colour don't cohere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreshortening and illusionistic perspective
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of foreshortening to create impressive illusionistic effects (e.g., figures 'foreshortened from below with an effect of marvellous grandeur').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate technical command of perspective and forced foreshortening to convey space and monumentality. Anti-pattern: incorrect perspective that flattens or distorts intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finish and delicacy of execution
rubrics_metrics.description: A graceful, delicate finish and attention to refined detail—'grace with which he finished his works', 'executed in detail with such exquisite finish'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vasari praises finish in small details (hair, ornament) and overall subtlety. Scoring: reward meticulous surface work and refined edges; penalize sloppiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expressiveness and emotional effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Paintings should move viewers emotionally—examples include a smiling boy whose expression makes observers smile, or devotional works inspiring veneration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the psychological presence and ability to evoke emotion. Examples: the Madonna and Child gestures; Christ scenes eliciting devotion. Anti-pattern: inert figures lacking expressive life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of light and shadow / atmospheric effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Skillful manipulation of light and shadow to create atmosphere—night effects, illumining angels, shadows that give force to sleeping apostles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: small night scene where an angel illumines Christ; mountain shadow giving force to figures. Evaluate clarity of light source, atmosphere, and how light shapes narrative and form. Anti-pattern: inconsistent lighting that confuses form or atmosphere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale control and patience in small formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to conceive and execute complex, convincing scenes even at small scale ('a foot square ... so well conceived ... no work of the same kind to equal it either in patience or in study').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vasari commends works that condense narrative and detail in miniature formats; assess fineness of finish, compositional coherence, and study evident in small works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative invention and theatrical staging
rubrics_metrics.description: Power to design spectacles and narrative presentations with grandeur, pomp, and dramatic effect (carnival processions, triumphal cars).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Piero's Carnival inventions and the Car of Death are cited as successful examples—criteria include orchestration of music, words, costumes, procession, and symbolic clarity. Reward integrated multi-disciplinary conception and effective public impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variety, richness of detail, and ornamentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Rich diversity in costumes, animals, instruments, architectural caprices, and ornamented borders—'diversity of the bay horses and garments' and 'various fanciful scenes of sacrifices in the ancient manner'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate inventiveness and convincing specificity in subsidiary details and ornament. Anti-pattern: monotonous or generic details that fail to enrich the scene.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trompe-l'oeil and deceptive realism
rubrics_metrics.description: Skill in counterfeiting objects (books, parchment) and tricks that deceive the eye ('counterfeited a book bound in parchment, somewhat old, which seems to be real').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessed by convincing illusionism of depicted objects and surfaces. Anti-pattern: poorly rendered imitations that reveal painterly artifice rather than objecthood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching influence and transmission of technique
rubrics_metrics.description: Artistic merit includes ability to teach or influence peers (e.g., Correggio teaching treatment of hair that opened eyes in Lombardy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vasari values innovators whose techniques are adopted by other painters; assess legacy, demonstrable technical contributions, and workshop impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency of vision vs. versatility
rubrics_metrics.description: Either a distinctive singular manner or valuable versatility is praised—Piero 'changed his manner almost for every work' while other passages praise a consistent perfected manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether stylistic changes show creative exploration and mastery (positive) or lack of coherent artistic identity (negative), depending on quality and intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study, diligence, and patience in execution
rubrics_metrics.description: Art requires long study and patient labour—works praised for 'patience and study', 'incredible patience', and 'diligence'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the evident labour, refinement, and time invested in composition and finish. Anti-pattern: rushed, superficial work without studied resolution.
